narrative.northStar: A conta de luz do seu mês
narrative.overview: Amigo do Bolso is built to look and read like a Brazilian utility bill. The ground is recycled bill paper, the ink is institutional deep blue, the numbers are a tabular monospace like a meter reading, and every section is a labeled ruled field. The one loud colour is not a brand colour — it is the bandeira tarifária, the verde/amarela/vermelha escalation flag every Brazilian reads on the electric bill. The design refuses the personal-finance category default: no fintech gradient, no donut dashboard, no giant balance number. The reading that matters is 'estou dentro do plano?' — a flag and a bar against a shared tick — and the raw reais are always secondary.
keyCharacteristics: Warm bill-paper ground with a faint diagonal security-tint hatch; institutional-blue ink.
One action colour (Amigo do Bolso orange), reserved for the single primary action.
The bandeira (green/amber/red) is functional-only and appears one flag per category.
Every monetary or measured value is tabular monospace; labels are small-caps official-notice type.
Near-square corners, ruled hairlines, perforated boleto-style dashed edges. Flat by default.

rules.name: The One Action Rule
rules.body: Orange marks exactly one thing per screen: the primary action, plus the active-state markers pointing at navigation. Never a decorative fill, a heading colour, or a second CTA.

rules.name: The Flag-Never-Alone Rule
rules.body: A bandeira colour never carries meaning by itself — always with its word (no verde/amarelo/vermelho), its percentage, and an inline flag pennant.

rules.name: The Two Grounds Rule
rules.body: Only two paper values exist: bill-paper for the page, panel-paper for anything raised. No third surface tone, no tinted category backgrounds behind content.

rules.name: The Meter-Reading Rule
rules.body: If a value is money or a measurement it is Spline Sans Mono with tabular-nums. Never a currency figure in Archivo, never running prose in the mono.

rules.name: The Notice-Label Rule
rules.body: Section titles and field labels are the small-caps notice-label, not heading-scale type. The label is the heading in a statement layout — a functional field label, never a decorative eyebrow.

rules.name: The Paper Rule
rules.body: Surfaces do not lift on hover. Interactive rows respond with a bg tint, never a shadow change or scale.

dos: Do set every R$ value, percentage, and measurement in Spline Sans Mono with tabular-nums.
Do pair every bandeira colour with its word and its % — colour is never the only signal.
Do keep all six category meters on the one shared scale: target at 72% of the track, always marked by the bare tick.
Do use the notice-label (uppercase, 0.09em, ink-muted) for section titles and field labels.
Do build sections as edge-to-edge bordered statement panels with a hairline header rule.
Do reserve action-orange (#ef7d24) for the single primary action and the active-nav markers.
Do keep surfaces flat — hover is a bg-secondary/40 tint, never a shadow or lift.
donts: Don't introduce a donut / pie chart, a fintech gradient, or a giant balance number as a screen hero.
Don't add a third paper tone or a tinted category background behind content.
Don't use action-orange as a decorative fill, a heading colour, or a second CTA on the same screen.
Don't set currency or data figures in Archivo, or running prose in the monospace.
Don't give category meters private scales — the shared 72% target tick is what makes them comparable.
Don't use rounded-full or pill shapes except the avatar; the system is near-square.
Don't reach for the AI-cluster rendition this world attracts (warm cream + serif display + terracotta).
